newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mixed, awaiting U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mixed, awaiting U.S. data.

text.p: U.S. shares trading in London were quiet and trendless on Thursday as investors chose to sit back and wait for U.S. economic data due later today for clues on the near-term direction of interest rates, dealers said.
"There is really no trend in the general market, everybody is using the figures as an excuse," said one trader.

U.S. blue chips climbed 36.56 points to 7,575.83 on Wednesday, their fourth consecutive all-time high. But investors were focusing on May retail sales data at 1230 GMT and weekly jobless claims estimated to total 326,000, ahead of the next FOMC meeting on July 2.
Among individual share movers, Archer Daniels Midland Co was trading at $20-5/8 down $1/4, following news that the company was the target of a price-fixing probe in Europe.
Philip Morris Cos Inc, which was due to go ex-dividend today, was down $1/8 at $42-3/4.
Reports that IBM chief financial officer Richard Thoman was expected to leave the group to run another company was not well received, traders said. IBM shares lost $1/2 to $86-3/4.
Shares in Coca-Cola and PepsiCo benefited from hopes that the pair would end the price war in the soft-drink industry.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Coca-Cola may seek to increase prices after July 4. The newspaper said the move was outlined in a memo distributed to company executives.
Shares in Coca Cola were trading up $1/4 at $68-3/4 and PepsiCo added $1/4 to $38.
Merck & Co rose gained $3/8 to $96-1/4 on the back of a study which has shown its new migraine drug Maxalt, provides faster and more complete pain relief that Glaxo Wellcome's remedy.
